newsitem.title: UK: Clarke to address UK Conservatives at 1120 GMT.
newsitem.headline: Clarke to address UK Conservatives at 1120 GMT.

text.p: British Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke will begin his keynote speech on the economy to the annual conference of the ruling Conservative Party at about 1120 GMT on Thursday, party officials said.

Aides to Clarke said the speech would contain no hints on the contents of next month's budget, which is seen by many Conservatives as crucial to their chances of winning a general election which must be held by next May.
They also said Clarke would merely reiterate government policy on the single European currency.

Prime Minister John Major has said a Conservative government would decide after the election whether it was in Britain's interests to join European monetary union and would hold a referendum if it decided to adopt the single currency.
Clarke gave a flavour of his speech in interviews with television and radio stations early on Thursday in which he said he would only cut taxes when that could be justified.
He said he was confident the Conservatives would win the election, and then cut taxes over a series of budgets. -- London Newsroom *44 171 5427767
